 Federal Board of Revenue President Upholds Decision to Introduce Faceless Income Tax Refund Regime
 Quratul Ain November 16, 2026 November 16, 2026 3 min read 
 ISLAMABAD: President Asif Ali Zardari has upheld a decision directing the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to introduce an automated and faceless income tax refund system under Section 170A of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001. The proposed system aims to speed up refund payments and reduce taxpayers’ interaction with tax offices.
 The President dismissed an FBR representation challenging an earlier decision in a case involving an outstanding income tax refund claim of Rs42.86 million for Tax Year 2025. However, the recommendation for introducing a Faceless Refund Regime was maintained.
 Under the proposed system, the FBR would automatically process eligible income tax refunds based on tax credits verified through its computerised system. Approved refund amounts would be transferred electronically into taxpayers’ registered bank accounts without requiring them to submit formal refund applications.
 The President observed that the FBR had already introduced faceless customs clearance and assessment systems. Similar arrangements should also be implemented for income tax refunds under Section 170A to improve efficiency and taxpayer facilitation.
 The decision also referred to the need for an appropriate mechanism through which verified tax credits could be processed automatically. This would reduce unnecessary paperwork, administrative delays and direct interaction between taxpayers and tax officials.
 Tax advisor Khurram Shahzad Butt welcomed the development, stating that an automated refund system could significantly reduce delays and improve taxpayer services. He maintained that unreasonable delays in processing legitimate refunds could amount to maladministration.
 He also referred to directions issued by the Islamabad High Court in Writ Petition No. 2173/2023, which called for an automated refund mechanism under Section 170A to minimise taxpayers’ interaction with tax offices and ensure faster payments.
 During the proceedings, the FBR argued that taxpayers could appeal against refund-related decisions before the Commissioner (Appeals) under Section 170(5) of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001. It also maintained that the refund claim in question was still undergoing verification.
 However, the argument that an appeal was available did not remove the tax authority’s responsibility to address administrative delays, according to the position presented by Khurram Shahzad Butt.
 The President’s decision has reinforced the recommendation that the FBR should develop and implement an automated, faceless refund mechanism.
 If implemented, the proposed system could bring significant changes to Pakistan’s income tax refund process.
 Taxpayers may no longer need to submit separate refund applications for amounts verified through the FBR’s computerised system. Instead, eligible refunds could be automatically approved and transferred to their notified bank accounts.
 The initiative is expected to reduce processing delays, improve transparency, minimise taxpayer interaction with tax offices and make the income tax refund process more efficient.
 However, the practical implementation will depend on the mechanism and procedures prescribed by the FBR under Section 170A.
